title: Go compiler parser (cmd/compile/internal/syntax/parser.go)
why: The Go compiler's own expression parser, showing each grammar production as the doc comment of a hand-written recursive-descent method and precedence passed as an argument.

title: go/parser parser core (src/go/parser/parser.go)
why: The standard library parser's parseBinaryExpr, a readable precedence-climbing loop to compare with the compiler's version.

title: go/parser entry points (src/go/parser/interface.go)
why: Documents the contract of ParseExpr/ParseExprFrom: what they return and the partial AST they produce for erroneous input.

title: Go runtime stack management (src/runtime/stack.go)
why: Shows in the runtime source when a goroutine stack is refused and the exact message printed, the mechanic behind parser stack-overflow reports.

title: runtime/debug SetMaxStack (src/runtime/debug/garbage.go)
why: The authoritative doc comment giving the default maximum goroutine stack size on 64-bit and 32-bit systems.

title: Clang binary expression parser (clang/lib/Parse/ParseExpr.cpp)
why: Clang's production precedence-climbing parser for binary and ternary operators, the C/C++ counterpart to the Go expression parsers.

claim: In the Go compiler's syntax package each grammar production is written as the doc comment of the hand-written method that implements it, here the expression production above binaryExpr.
quote:
// Expression = UnaryExpr | Expression binary_op Expression .
func (p *parser) binaryExpr(x Expr, prec int) Expr {

claim: binaryExpr loops while the pending operator's precedence p.prec is greater than the prec argument, and for each operator parses its right operand by calling itself with that operator's own precedence tprec.
quote:
for (p.tok == _Operator || p.tok == _Star) && p.prec > prec {
		t := new(Operation)
		t.pos = p.pos()
		t.Op = p.op
		tprec := p.prec
		p.next()
		t.X = x
		t.Y = p.binaryExpr(nil, tprec)

claim: ParseExpr returns an ast.Expr and an error, delegating to ParseExprFrom(token.NewFileSet(), "", []byte(x), 0), and when syntax errors were found the result is a partial AST containing ast.Bad nodes, with multiple errors returned as a source-position-sorted scanner.ErrorList.

go/parser's parseBinaryExpr returns the accumulated left operand once the next token's operator precedence oprec is below prec1, and otherwise parses the right operand by recursing with precedence oprec+1.
The file-level comment of ParseExpr.cpp describes the code it contains as a simple precedence-based parser for binary and ternary operators.
quote: /// Simple precedence-based parser for binary/ternary operators.

claim: Clang parses binary expressions with ParseRHSOfBinaryExpression, which takes the already-parsed left-hand side LHS together with a minimum precedence MinPrec.

SetMaxStack sets the maximum memory a single goroutine stack may use and the program crashes if any goroutine exceeds that limit while growing its stack; SetMaxStack returns the previous setting and its initial value is 1 GB on 64-bit systems and 250 MB on 32-bit systems.

When the newly computed stack size would exceed maxstacksize or maxstackceiling, the runtime prints "runtime: goroutine stack exceeds <N>-byte limit", where N is maxstacksize if maxstacksize is smaller than maxstackceiling and maxstackceiling otherwise.
